readout_other: Digiscan-16 automated animal activity monitor (horizontal/vertical activity counts); nNOS immunohistochemistry cell counts in spinal cord laminae
direction_notes: US treatment significantly suppressed the CFA-induced increase in the number of spinal nNOS-immunoreactive neurons bilaterally in all laminae compared with sham treatment.

exposures.label: Therapeutic pulsed ultrasound applied to the CFA-injected (arthritic) hindlimb

target.label: tibiotarsal joint (ankle) of the CFA-injected right hindpaw

timing.protocol_description: One-megahertz–pulsed US with an on/off ratio of 1:1 (ie, 2ms of US on, 2ms off) was applied for 5 minutes at an intensity of 1.0W/cm2, delivered via a commercial device (US-3) with a treatment head 1.7cm in diameter and effective radiating area 0.75cm2.

source_quotes.n_subjects: Eighteen hours after CFA induction, all 10 arthritic animals were slightly anesthetized with ethyl ether by inhalation and were randomly divided into 2 groups of 5 animals each: 1 group to receive US treatment and the other to receive sham treatment, which consisted of placing US apparatus on the hind limb but not delivering US output.

flags.reason: Ultrasound was applied to the arthritic ankle/hindpaw joint, not to a nervous-system structure in the target vocabulary; classified as 'other'.
Paper models CFA-induced monoarthritis/inflammatory pain in the rat hindpaw; mapped to the closest available vocabulary term (chronic_pain) rather than a literal 'arthritis' category.

Paper states a single device output 'intensity' of 1.0 W/cm2 without specifying whether this is ISPTA or ISATA, or whether it was measured in water or at the skin/tissue surface; placed in unspecified_domain.
PRF (250 Hz) derived from the stated on/off period (2 ms on + 2 ms off = 4 ms period), a unit conversion from the stated period rather than computed arithmetic.
